summary: Karl Brunnhölzl works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (attested 2009), Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Lama Thubten.

Specializing in Tibetology and history and archaeology, Karl Debreczeny earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung and teacher Jenny Purtle. He served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Uppsala University in 1880. He later served there as University Professor of Sanskrit and the Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages from circa 1893 to 1925.

Working in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics, Karl Florenz served as a professor at the University of Tokyo from circa 1891 to 1914 and held a post at the University of Hamburg from circa 1914 to 1934.

Karl Friedrich Geldner specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen and Leipzig under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Brockhaus, and Ernst Windisch, holding posts at Tübingen, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Marburg.

Karl H. Potter was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Harvard University in 1955. He served as a professor at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1970) and later held a professorship at the University of Washington (attested 1987–1999).

Karl Hoffmann was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Saarland University (~1952–1955) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he served as professor from circa 1955 to 1983.

Karl Jettmar specialized in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held academic posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from circa 1961 to 1964 and at Heidelberg University from circa 1964 to 1983.

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, Heidelberg University, and the University of Halle-Wittenberg between 1824 and 1828. He later held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1828 to 1833.
Karl Verner was a linguist who studied at Aarhus Katedralskole. He later held a post at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1883 until 1896.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at LMU Munich (~1970–1977). He held posts at LMU Munich, the Ifo Institute, and became a professor in 1992 at both FH Würzburg-Schweinfurt and the Munich School of Politics.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo earned a doctorate from the University of Hawaii (~1990–2000) and held posts at the University of San Diego, Chaminade University, and UC San Diego. She founded Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women and directed the Jamyang Foundation.

Karma Phuntsho is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford, completing his PhD under Michael Aris, and was mentored by David Seyfort Ruegg, later holding a postdoctoral position at CNRS (~2003–2005).

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She completed a Shastri and Acharya at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, followed by a PhD at the University of Tasmania supervised by Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Working in Tibetology, Karma Ura completed an undergraduate degree at Magdalen College, Oxford (~1983–1986) and a graduate degree at the University of Edinburgh (~1987–1989). He became Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies circa 1999.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Karunesh Shukla is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation (attested 1991). He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1991).

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Allahabad and Jesus College, Oxford (~1906–1910). In 1917, he served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. In 1937, he served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India, succeeding Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai from circa 1864 to 1869. He served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone College from circa 1868 to 1872.
